members.name: Worker
members.doc: From a function: its source is sent (never the value), `w.call(...args)` runs it; what it uses must be a `fogu:` module, a top-level function or a constant — a captured local is an error naming it. A program of its own on another OS thread, with its own interpreter — on CPU `core` if given: the way to use several cores (`fg` tasks share one thread). `w.call(name, ...args)` calls a global function of the worker and waits without stopping the other tasks; arguments and results cross as JSON (numbers, texts, bools, nil, lists, maps) and nothing else is shared. A failure of the call comes back as an error value. Each worker is a thread of the same process, not a separate process: its own interpreter, heap of Fogu values, task scheduler and socket reactor, so workers scale over cores without locks. With `net.tcpListen(addr, { reusePort: true })` in each, a TCP server uses every core (`bench/net/tcp_workers.fg`). `w.close()`, fields `core source closed`.

modules.name: password
modules.summary: Password storage. `hash` and `verify` are slow on purpose and run off the interpreter thread, so other `fg` tasks keep running. The salt is always random (16 bytes). Defaults follow the OWASP Password Storage Cheat Sheet: argon2id m=19456 KiB t=2 p=1 · bcrypt cost 12 · scrypt N=2 17 r=8 p=1 · PBKDF2-SHA256 600 000 / PBKDF2-SHA512 210 000 iterations.

members.name: hash
members.signature: password.hash(pw, { algorithm, memory, time, parallelism, cost, n, r, p, iterations, pepper })
members.doc: `algorithm`: `argon2id` (default), `argon2i`, `argon2d`, `bcrypt`, `scrypt`, `pbkdf2-sha256`, `pbkdf2-sha512`. argon2: `memory` (KiB), `time`, `parallelism`; bcrypt: `cost` 4..20; scrypt: `n` (power of two), `r`, `p`; PBKDF2: `iterations`. Costs beyond any recommended setting are refused, for new and stored hashes alike: argon2 memory above 2 GiB or memory × time above 8 GiB, scrypt above 2 GiB of memory or 8 GiB of work, bcrypt cost above 20, more than 20 000 000 PBKDF2 iterations. Returns a PHC string (`$argon2id$…`, `$scrypt$…`, `$pbkdf2-sha256$…`) or bcrypt's `$2b$…`. Unknown options stop the program.

members.name: verify
members.doc: Detects the algorithm from the hash (`$argon2id$`, `$2a$`/`$2b$`/`$2y$`, `$scrypt$`, `$pbkdf2-sha256$`…); constant-time comparison. A malformed or unsupported hash, or one whose parameters are too large (a hash with `m=4294967295` would abort the process) → error value. Accepts the same options map as `hash`.

members.name: serve
members.signature: http.serve(port | "ip:port", fn(req), { tls: { cert, key }, quiet, maxBody, maxHeaderBytes, headerTimeout, readTimeout, handlerTimeout }?)
members.doc: `tls` serves HTTPS (see [fogu:tls](#fogutls)). The handler returns a response (`http.text/json/html`), a str (text), any other value (JSON), nil (404) or an `error` (logged; the client gets a 500). Limits (defaults): `maxBody` (10 MB, 413), `maxHeaderBytes` (64 KB for the request line and headers, 431), `headerTimeout` (30s to send the headers; also closes idle keep-alive connections), `readTimeout` (60s for the body, 408), `handlerTimeout` (60s for the program's answer, 504; `0` = none). The request path is made canonical once, before static files, middlewares and routes see it: decoded once (`+` stays `+`), repeated slashes collapsed, `.`/`..` resolved; an encoded `/` or `\`, a raw `\`, a control character or a `..` above the root is a 400. A Rust panic in a handler answers that request with a 500 and the server goes on. Several servers may run in one program. Requests are answered as soon as they arrive while the program is alive — waiting in `Fogu.signal.wait()`, `time.delay`, on a channel… — and each handler runs in its own task, so one that waits does not hold the others. The address is an int port (on 127.0.0.1) or `"0.0.0.0:8080"`, `"[::1]:8080"`, `":8080"`.
